_comment: CrisperWhisper 2.0 per-tensor tolerances for compare_tensors.py.
CORRECTNESS REGIME (every number below was measured in exactly this one):
reference : crisperwhisper 2.0.2, transformers backend, BF16 weights
upcast to F32 compute (compute_type=float32), eager attention,
CPU, torch-threads=1, greedy, all three rewind features OFF.
C++       : crisperwhisper-2.0-small-F32.gguf, --backend cpu --threads 1
--kv-type f32, production C++ MelFrontend (no ref-mel injection).
cases     : jfk (clean read speech) + disfluency (filler/cutoff/repetition);
each entry takes the max over both.
WHY THE GATE USES THE F32 GGUF WHILE THE FAMILY SHIPS BF16:
BF16 -> F32 is lossless, so the F32 GGUF holds values identical to the
shipped BF16 file; what differs is the kernel. ggml's BF16 path sets
vec_dot_type=GGML_TYPE_BF16 with from_float=ggml_cpu_fp32_to_bf16, so it
rounds ACTIVATIONS to BF16 before every dot product, which torch at F32
does not. Measured three pairings on enc.block.6.out:
F32 oracle  / F32 GGUF    1.66e-02   <- this file
F32 oracle  / BF16 GGUF   12.76
BF16 oracle / BF16 GGUF   71.13
BF16-on-both-sides is the WORST pairing, because torch at dtype=bfloat16
stores every activation in BF16 (residual stream and embedding table
included) while ggml keeps the graph in F32 and rounds only mul_mat src1.
It also destroys the exact 0.0 on the pure-read tensors. So the gate
measures graph correctness here, and the precision cost of the shipped
BF16 artifact is measured on WER at Stage 4 Step 11 instead.
The manifest pins this via validation.gguf_quant / validation.kv_type.
ZERO-DRIFT ENTRIES (pinned at exact 0.0, not the 1e-6 floor):
dec.token_emb / dec.pos_emb / enc.pos_emb are pure GGUF reads and
dec.embed_sum is their pure F32 add. All four measure exactly 0.0.
Any nonzero value here means an unintended dtype conversion crept into
the lookup/add path - investigate, do not absorb.
WIDENED vs the Stage 2 provisional budget (4 entries, all encoder residual):
enc.block.{6,8,11}.out  35x,  enc.final  4.8x.
Mechanism: NOT extra drift. The provisional formula scales by p99_abs,
which badly under-represents these tensors because Whisper's encoder
carries outlier channels - max|x| is ~800 where p99_abs is 4.3, a 180x
gap. Relative to the actual peak the observed drift is 1.9e-05
(enc.final 7.0e-05), i.e. TIGHTER than the 1e-4 relative budget the
provisional formula was aiming for. Absolute drift is flat across
blocks 6/8/11 (1.53e-02 each), consistent with a fixed rounding
difference riding the residual stream rather than accumulation.
MODE-TAG AND WORD-TIMING GATES (both now measured, nothing provisional):
dec.intended.logits_raw : a second prompt pass in the OTHER mode, mirroring
the reference dumper's sibling pass. It proves the
[verbatim_N]/[intended_N] tags are a real control
surface, not decoration.
dec.xattn.align         : head-averaged cross-attention, one row per
PREDICTED token including the row that emits EOT,
which is why it is one row longer than the
generated text. Post-softmax, so drift is ~1e-07.

dec.embed_sum._exact: pure GGUF read / pure F32 add - measured exactly 0.0
